newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU rules drive animal health industry away - survey.
newsitem.headline: EU rules drive animal health industry away - survey.

text.p: Excessive restrictions are driving an increasing number of animal health companies to relocate research and production plants outside Western Europe, a new survey said on Thursday.
Some 60,000 people are directly employed in the animal health industry which is of great importance for the 100 billion Ecus a year international livestock sector providing some seven million jobs.

The survey on "Benchmarking and Competitiveness of the European Animal Health Industry in Europe" identified serious hurdles to developing new products and competing with U.S. and the rest of the world.

"These obstacles are excessive restriction from over-zealous regulations, delays in processing product licensing applications and disproportionately high costs of product clearance," said the survey for the European Federation of Animal Health (FEDESA).
An estimated 60 percent of animal health companies have created new research and development facilities outside Europe, mainly to escape excessive red tape.
But FEDESA President Robert Marsboom told a news briefing to mark the survey's launch that the industry supported rules based on sound science as they helped to boost consumer confidence.

Marsboom added that the industry welcomed efforts by EU Food Safety Commissioner Emma Bonino to improve food safety in the wake of the mad cow crisis, especially stricter enforcement of EU rules and controls.
"It creates a level playing field," he said.
